title: Prevalence of Female and Male Athlete Triad Risk Factors in Ultramarathon Runners
authors: Hoeg TB, Olson EM, Skaggs K, Sainani K, Fredericson M, Roche M, Kraus E
population: 123 runners (83 male, 40 female; mean ages 46.2 and 41.8) recruited at a 100-mile ultramarathon in 2018 and 2019
findings: Elevated disordered-eating risk in 62.5% of women and 44.5% of men.
History of BSI in 37.5% of women and 20.5% of men; BMD Z-score below -1.0 in 16.7% of women and 30.1% of men.
Low BMI (below 18.5 kg/m2) in 15% of women and no men.
Triad Cumulative Risk Assessment: moderate risk in 61.1% of women and 29.2% of men; high risk in 5.6% of both. Disordered-eating risk was not associated with low BMD or low BMI.
limitations: Cross-sectional volunteers at one race; only 40 women; self-reported BSI history; ferritin and vitamin D collected in 2019 only.
implications: Do not assume recreational ultra runners are low risk: include the REDs/triad screen and bone stress history question for both sexes in 100-mile plans.
Low BMD was more common in men here, so the bone-health prompt must not be limited to women.
Do not use BMI alone as a gate; disordered-eating risk was not associated with low BMI or BMD.

verification.notes: Crossref matches (Clin J Sport Med; online 2021-07, issue year 2022; first author Hoeg). Percentages confirmed in Europe PMC abstract (PMID 34232162).
